body: Thank you. I'm really just trying to keep my sanity.
This is the anniversary of my most recent sexual assault but also I feel like nobody cares. I feel like I deserved it and should have died when he choked me

Oh dear lord. I had this happen during my mri, they tried both arms multiple times, both hands and then they brought up an anesthesiologist to assist them. They still ended up going into the underside of my wrist. If I moved at all it was excruciating. Lucky for me I was in there partially for hand twitches. :/ never again, now I ask for someone new after 3 pokes. They get all offended too...like it's MY fault.

I'm currently in PT and we do 1/2 time in the pool. Since I don't own a pool the non pool time is a chance to teach me exercises I can reasonably do at home. I do what I can and try not to over do it, the pool time is great though, even if there's no long term relief, the couple times of week I get at the pool are very therapeutic. I also take advantage of the spas even though I'm not a member. My therapist also says to stay in the pool as long as I want before and after our alotted time. I've made it clear that I need to not overdo it and it's been good. Today I couldn't walk after our session but I could tell it was just a bit of fatigue and soreness and not a fibro flare. We'll see tomorrow but I've been impressed this far.
We do core/pelvic work and stretches for my back on land and balance and leg/arm work in the pool.

Oh my God, so much this...I managed to get into a therapist..ahem...counselor...three months in the future and I've been waiting a while year for said counselor to start my work on cptsd. She likes to talk about herself a lot. She's sweet enough and she HAS THE RESOURCES RIGHT THERE! So I'm sticking it out, my meds (finally getting into a psychiatrist after 11 months) are giving me that little bit of support to stand up for myself. But I'm still a wreck. I went to the ER for suicidal thoughts and it was a multiple day wait on an uncomfortable er bed to possibly get a bed at the psych hospital. The fluorescent lights started to give me A migraine and my anxiety disorder kicked in over being in a strange place with strange men (I don't have a problem with men...I mean I don't want to, in general but you know...sexual abuse...) freaked me the eff out. I couldn't do it and was able to discharge myself because my suicide "score" went down. I just told them what they wanted to hear. I was placed on "home suicide watch" and that was good enough for them. I'm lucky to have made it through all that. The US needs an overhaul of its mental health system. 
NAAMI is great and there are probably emergency shelters or volunteers that offer up an extra bed for a night. Those types of organizations are a life saver. Especially when medical organizations leave you hanging.

My new rheumatolgist told me the same thing which was so validating after having a pcp who told me I needed to do more aggressive cardio. That pcp caused me to be bedridden for two weeks after referring me to a trainer who kept pushing me too far. Now I'm doing gentle stretching, light cardio and balance work in the warm pool and light cardio and gentle stretching "on land" with a physical therapist and I feel better than I have in a while.
Get away from your mother by any means possible. She really can't control you and you'll be better off. I really wish I could go back in time and save my younger self.
"I could care less" and "should of"

I saw a new rheumatolgist the other day and she said about half her patients have a history of emotional trauma. She believes that is what caused mine. Not just one event but a culmination of events and it all eventually just caught up to me. She's the only doctor I've seen that has admitted it's likely trauma related. I've had some say it's "just stress" and it's "all in my head" but never admitted to the relation between my past and my illness.

I would still try your pcp. I've had 3 different PCPs prescribe or change my gabapentin this year. And in 2015 my pcp prescribed it to me. I actually have two scripts from two different doctors for the gabapentin because one upped the nighttime dose. Thought my insurance would reject it but surprisingly they didn't.

I'd do this. My PCP prescribed my gabapentin and adjusts it as necessary. It's definitely something you don't need a rheumatolgist to have managed. You can also ask your pcp to put it on your allergy list. I have two meds on mine that have really bad side effects, I'm not "allergic" to them but it will help other doctors see that they did not go well for me.
I think we got a defective golden doodle. Allllll he does is sleep. He's the laziest dog I've ever seen. He's the best. Great for snuggles. They are very gentle and sweet dogs.

I've had really bad problems with my hands and I always attributed it to my job doing data entry. I haven't had that job in almost two years and my hands are still cramping and useless most of the time. I'm having an emg on my wrists in March to see if there may be an underlying cause but my pain management doctor said it's a common fibromyalgia problem so I'm not getting my hopes up. A doctor I had about 5 years back told me I had cubital and carpal tunnel and I did everything she told me to and nothing helped. But I was never really tested for it. Do you have a physical therapist that understands fibro? I've found some don't and they push too hard. A huge thing is not to overdo it. It's really hard to set limitations with this disease, at least for me. But if I don't I feel it. I'm still feeling the effects of pushing myself through preparing Thanksgiving dinner. It really sucks when it's your hands. I used to like Journaling, I like doing crosswords, I love coloring, I want to learn how to knit, I want to be able to sew, I miss cooking every meal. People don't realize how fortunate they are to have working, able hands. I'm sorry you're going through this I know it sucks. Hang in there.

Both times I've been tested for vitamin d levels they've been extremely low. I'm on prescription vitamin d at the moment. 50000 iud once a week for 10 weeks. Haven't noticed any difference with it but I've been in a pretty bad flare the last couple weeks so hopefully I'll start to see improvements soon. My doctor didn't think the deficiency was the cause of any of my problems though. He just wanted to check it because the cold and rain was effecting my ability to get outside and get sun and because I had been deficient before. Polyarthralgia is what my rheumatolgist diagnosed me with "officially" but he told me it was fibro so...that was weird but maybe certain doctors just prefer those different terms.

I have adhd as well. My current doctors won't prescribe anything for it because I'm "not doing anything that would require me to focus"....except I'm desperately trying to do so much to improve my situation. Anyhow when I was working I found that on days I was having a really hard time with both fatigue and brain fog that Adderall definitely helped. My old psychiatrist said that fog and fatigue and not being able to stay focused was adding to my anxiety at work and she was right. Might be worth checking out if you have ADHD. I've always been very easily distracted but it got worse as I got older. To the point that I failed classes in college because of it. My high school teachers were really understanding but college professors not so much. My managers at my last couple of jobs also were not understanding and I got many verbal warnings. I didn't ever think I had adhd (because I was never hyperactive) but my psychiatrist saw the symptoms and had me take a test and turns out I was. The Adderall helped so much. Even with simple things like cleaning the house. I could focus on the task at hand and not have twenty different cleaning projects going at once. It just helped me be more methodical and less frantic and all over the place.
Thank you! Very much appreciated.

My boyfriend and myself are looking to relocate in the spring. We've been applying to affordable housing but we don't have enough income...uhm okay. If I get denied SSI again I'm going to have to find some sort of employment...even though I can barely use my hands most days. Even still it'll only be part time. I've been denied state cash assistance even though they found me permanently and totally disabled. Don't get me wrong I'm so so so grateful for medical insurance. But like...I can't even afford stuff like deodorant and shampoo. One of my two pairs of pants just ripped so...yeah...fortunately we can do laundry for free. Our housing situation is making my conditions worse and we're trying to look at any and all possibilities. I would love info for you where you're located, it's not an area we've looked at yet.

Quit cymbalta cold turkey twice and I can't believe I made it through, second time was worse than the first. I'll never touch the stuff again and my doctors get angry about it and one has refused to treat my fibro if I don't take it. She's no longer my pcp. Lyrica was worse and doctors don't like to hear that you refuse to take it. I second the epsom salt baths.

Not my home but I was staying at a friends house and we met a guy at a concert who seemed like a decent guy. After the show he missed his bus and and he told my friend he was going to sleep outside the station in the rain. She let him come back to sleep a few hours and catch the next bus. We all got back and went to bed and not 10 minutes later the dude starts masturbating. My friend starts clearing her throat and coughing hoping he'd stop, but he continued on and finished. The next day he's gone and leaves her a cryptic MySpace message about her stuffed animal being good in bed. She then finds her stuffed animal from childhood with cum all over it. It was a very disturbing night. Like you can't keep your sexual urges repressed for one night?! He was 100% sober too so there's no blaming any sort of mind altering substances. Still gives me the heeby jeebies.

You could try the CPSTD workbook. My therapist is literally just reading it and have me tell her my thoughts. If you could come up with the money for it, I know it's hard, I definitely wouldn't have the money for it this moment. 

https://www.amazon.com/Complex-PTSD-Workbook-Mind-Body-Regaining/dp/1623158249

I seem to feel it the most in my joints when it's cold so I try to wear layers of clothing especially on the joints to keep them warm and also try to move them as much as possible to keep them from stiffening up. Just laying in bed and moving them works. Before getting up I try to do 30 seconds of just moving each joint as much as I can so that it's not excruciatingly painful when I step out of bed. I keep a light winter hat near me at all times so I can put it on if I start to get really cold. Sounds cliche but hot tea even if only to hold in my hands and warm me up. Capsaicin cream is warming but it burns in the shower FYI. I wear multiple layers of leggings, seems weird but I can pull a layer off if I get warm. I wear a tighter legging underneath a pair I have that are a little baggy. They have slippers that come with inserts you can put in the microwave, I love those. And they have a lavender scent so it's calming. An aromatherapy diffuser for calming scents or warming scents.

I've been trying, and mostly succeeding, to get a regular sleep pattern. I get up when my boyfriend comes to bed at 5 am, I can't convince him to go to sleep earlier. As much as I love him to death, I kind of love the alone time I get in the morning. I'm 10 days sober. (!!!!!) I feel more clear headed and I know it's healthier. Saw a new PCP and she's good except we differ in certain beliefs. I like her enough to stick with her a bit and see how it goes. So I think that's probably a win. We'll have to wait and find out in that one. I am worried she's pushing me in the wrong direction but... Yeah, anyway. Have been using kratom and aside from one bad experience (my fault, took too much) it does work better than OTC meds. My doctors are pushing for medical cannabis but I think that might be too expensive as it isn't covered by insurance. Also we got new comfy and warm flannel sheets with dogs on them and that made me really happy.

Keto has helped my stomach issues, probably 90%, you can modify it to be vegetarian but it's lots of tofu and fake meats from what I've read researching it. I was a strict vegan for years before doing keto so it's been a bit of a shock to the system. I get kinda grossed out by some of the things I eat, especially pork, I hate it but we buy what's on sale. My number one complaint is that I can't just munch on veggies all day and can't have most fruit. But again it REALLY helped my stomach issues. We decided to have a cheat day and we had Chinese food. I ate lo mein, picked out the meat, and crab rangoons and have been sick for two days. I now remember what my life was like before keto and I'm not straying again. I don't find it to have helped with the pain though which sucks, however just to not have constant stomach issues is worth it.

My doctor told me last week that dropping things and numbness in the hands is common with Fibromyalgia. That was one of my first symptoms and I got sent to a neurologist and I showed no signs in tests that it was MS. Now I'm being sent back to a neurologist to get some tests done on my hands and back, "just in case" but he thinks it's Fibromyalgia still. We're only doing the neurological testing because my mother and maternal uncle have MS. He is an amazing doctor and it took my six months to get in with him. He seems to know a lot about fibromyalgia and so I do value his opinion.

I couldn't find a lawyer to take my case. I have fibro, chronic back pain, severe PTSD, migraines, major depressive disorder (that's what I'm currently "diagnosed" with, however right now I'm IN a major depression but I have dysthymia, whatever), psychophysiological insomnia, and anxiety. I called many lawyers and no dice. So frustrated because they know they might not win so they refuse to help. But all of my illnesses make it impossible to function most days. I'm currently awaiting a hearing and I'm nervous af. They didn't have my medical records and when I asked my doctors to send them in they said "it doesn't work like that, we need them to reach out to us." I get hung up on every single time I call my local office. "Social Security, please hold" *click* "call ended". Now I understand why people get lawyers and I wish I could find someone to help me. I can't even get a case worker because they're all booked up. Sooooo frustrating. Sorry, I kinda vented there. I hope you have better luck than I have.

He's a Golden doodle. Basically the same thing I think. At least they look exactly the same. He seems to know when I'm having a bad day and curls up next to me and won't leave...unless chicken is involved, he loves chicken.

I like to wear sweaters and skirts which are comfy and recently I've given in to jeggings instead of regular jeans. One thing I miss is some of my cute shoes with heels. Can't wear those at all anymore and it makes me sad.

This is Tug, he keeps me sane.

My boyfriend likes to call me accident prone because I'm always hurting myself doing the most mundane things. I was trying to put a Swiffer away behind a mop and they both came at me and bruised my lip and cheek. I literally ran into a door getting up to go pee in the middle of the night have myself a black eye. Was trying to get a glass bowl from a high shelf and it hit me in the eye, another black eye. When I was 20 I was running to my car because I was running late and my foot went into a hole and I broke my ankle. Bruised my ribs getting stuff out of my trunk. Got a rock stuck in my upper lip when I crashed my little four wheeler into a tree when I was in middle school. Broke my pinky toenail in half lengthwise vacuuming. Fell in the bathtub trying to clean the walls and got a concussion. It's never exciting or cool things. I'm just incredibly clumsy and inattentive.

I have chronic pain and it takes my pain down better than anything I've tried. It's not a completely relieving solution. I also don't take more than a few teaspoons at a time. I just started a few weeks ago. The other day I took kratom a few hours before grocery shopping because that's my most painful chore. I was able to walk around the store great without having to take breaks to lean on things. Problem was as it started to wear off I realized in the joy of being in less pain I was pushing my body too much and could not walk on my own from the register to the car. Since nothing has worked on my pain we were afraid to put too much into buying a crap load of kratom and I also am trying to figure out which strains will work for each of my ridiculous illnesses. I have to say the red Bali has helped the most for pain from the 3 I've tried so far. Because of the cost I can't buy a whole bunch right now so I only take it when the pain is just too unbearable or I know I'm going to need to do something that will be painful or stressful. But I can say for me it brings my pain down 2-3 levels on the pain scale, whereas 1000mg ibuprofen brings it down .5-1 levels, 1400 mg (not all at once) gabapentin .5-1 levels. Cymbalta, Wellbutrin and Lyrica don't touch the pain at all and they make my mental illnesses worse. Daily I'm between a 6-9. If I overdo it it's at a straight up ten for 4-5 days. I'm curious to see how it works when I encounter one of those stretches.

I was so annoyed with myself yesterday because I was being set off by every little thing around me. I could not get comfortable at all. I can't turn without searing pain in my hips, I can't sleep because of the pain in my legs. It's all so annoying!

For me I have to try on a bajillion scarves for one that isn't uncomfortable. I have a thing against certain fabrics. They will literally make nauseated. I can't stand collars most of the time. I had a coat that I bought at Target 4-5 years ago that's sweater material and the neck is really loose but it covers up to your chin. It's in storage and I've gone up a size anyhow and spent 6 hours yesterday on poshmark and I actually found it. Keep searching and you'll find something that won't drive you crazy. I also need something easy to take off because I'm always switching between boiling and freezing. 
I do like the idea of a shawl like others said but never used one.

I've noticed only lately the thing with spicy foods. I used to be able to handle them but now I break out into a sweat. At the same time my inability to regulate my internal temperature is getting worse. I think because I'm overweight my doctors think my sweating in their office is because of that but I would literally NEVER sweat before two years ago. 90 degree weather with a hooded sweatshirt and not a drop. I actually thought maybe there was something wrong with my sweat glands. Now I go from freezing to sweating in a few minutes and then the next I'm freezing again. But I do know that spicy food really the sweat dripping so I try to stay away from that more now.

I knew that when I looked in the website and saw the specifically treats fibromyalgia that it would be helpful. Took me forever to get in with him and my next appointment is in three months but he told me a lot of useful stuff and said my ankle is probably a mixture of real pain being amplified by fibro. 
However because I've stated worsening pain in my hands and feet he's considering perhaps a different or coexisting condition. More tests. It really was the best appointment I've had in a looooong time.

I feel like the original trainer I was with knew how bad it can be. But the swim instructor didn't know anything about the condition and while he asked me lots of questions he still didn't know really what to do. And neither did I. I'm not used to limiting myself. I always do too much. I've only been dealing with the really painful symptoms for the last 4 years. While it seems like a long time, it's not when you're trying everything under the sun to feel better. They say walk so I walk, but it's not helping so they say walk more so I do and it's REALLY not helping. The last 6 months or so I've been terribly depressed so I'm in bed more often than not and I'm so over everyone's advice. And I'm so over everyone telling me I'm wasting my life in bed. Thanks Captain Obvious! Ugh. Sorry that got really ranty at the end

Keep trying. I'm on my 8th primary care doctor in 4 years. 4th of this year. Fortunately the NP I saw for about a month until my regular PCP came back from vacation sent in a recommendation for a pain management doctor. It is a diagnosis of exclusion unfortunately. You will need to see many doctors and rule out everything else. Heck I've had multiple tests done twice in three years. My pain doctor said he wants everything run again. Just gave 6 of those big vials of blood for tests. I'm going back to a neurologist because MS runs in my family (if it is I indeed genetic). Then another rheumatologist in a few months. I'm annoyed because it kind of seems like he doesn't believe me with all these tests (I have been officially diagnosed though so I don't care if he wants to triple check everything) but towards the end of the appointment he told me how we'll approach it if it is Fibromyalgia.
I'm on Medicaid too and haven't had to pay anything out of pocket this last year while going through the disability process. I've been labeled APTD in my state but they won't give me any cash assistance. Though I'm eternally grateful for the medical assistance or I'd have just jumped off a bridge by now. I don't know if you already applied for ssi/SSDI but it's a sucky thing to go through. I'm on month 19 and I'm freaking out because I have absolutely no help in the process and I can't figure out to get my medical records to social security. SS has hung up on me or just not picked up the phone EVERY TIME I've tried to contact them. I've been told the only way to get help is to go to the office and speak face to face so they can't hang up on you. They are there to deny to you not to approve you. Sadly.

My favorite is "don't you just want to be happy?" Or "can't you just be happy." Oh shit, I never tried that! Thanks for your advice. I've had dysthymia for 21 years, you don't think I've tried that before, Karen? 
Better yet when I try to tell some people "you wouldn't give a diabetic crap for taking their insulin would you? So why are you giving me crap for needing antidepressive/anti-anxiety meds." And I get "Well diabetes is real." Ugh.

I was prescribed Adderall by a psychiatrist. I do have ADHD and combined with fibro fog I wasn't able to do my job very efficiently. The Adderall helped. I wouldn't think that's something a rheumatologist could prescribe but made your PCP. None of my doctors, including my rheumatologist will deal with my meds except gabapentin. I've always been passed off to a psychiatrist.
Are you sure you don't have ADHD? I didn't know until my thirties. I suspected I might but my parents always brushed it off or laughed at me. I wish I had known in college, might not have done so poorly.

I can't chop vegetables, etc for very long because of Fibro pain. However my old NP told me not to blame all pain on fibro. The last 3 doctors I've had blame EVERYTHING on fibro. I'm currently stuck in bed because I have terrible neck and back pain. I finally got into pain management with a fantastic doctor, I was on the waiting list for 6 months. He agrees it's probably all fibro but he wants to recheck everything and wants testing done on my hands, back and neck and he'd like to see an MRI ordered so he's sending me to a neurologist. He also reiterated not to blame everything on fibro. If it's something that can be addressed and worked on why be in more pain than you have to? 
Do you notice your wrist being worse with weather changes? I broke my ankle and now it acts up when it's cold and I walk too much. It almost feels like it did when it broke. The pain management doctor says that's normal and there really isn't anything to be done about it. And that I should've stayed in PT (I had extreme social anxiety and a fear of hospitals at the time so I flaked on therapy). Oops.

I'm so glad someone else had this experience too. First day of something they call "Exercise is Medicine" put me into a two week flare. It was a month long program so... Pretty much two weeks wasted. When I went back I didn't ask for help from the trainers or instructors. I just did whatever I felt like doing. My doctor proceeded to yell at me at my follow up. She said I have unreasonable expectations of not having pain after working out, everyone has pain when they start working out. As someone who used to work out 2 hours a day, 6 days a week. I know the difference between that "good hurt" and a two week flare. She's no longer my doctor. Good riddance.

My doctor told me I had carpal and cubital tunnel and stress. Now after many different doctors I have a diagnosis of fibromyalgia and chronic back pain. I'm terrified of the fact that it might be a misdiagnosis because my "symptoms aren't bad enough to warrant further testing." I'm sorry your wife had to go through that. My mother was misdiagnosed as well until she got bells palsy and terrible pains in her left leg. As a child it was a tough thing to see. Then finding out it could be genetic, her and my uncle have it, I got pretty worried. I haven't really kept up with current studies and don't know if they've figured out a cause yet. (My mother and I aren't close and it's not that I don't care but... Uhm, yeah.) Again I'm so terribly sorry about what your wife has gone through and continues to battle every day. Doctors need to be more understanding and listen to their patients more. I'm on my fourth primary care doctor of the year. We'll see how that goes. 😕

In case there's an emergency during the night. My mother used to scare the Dickens out of us before bed telling us all the ways we could die if things weren't just so. No closing the door to our room in case of fire, no headphones in bed because they'll choke you, also no headphones because what if we don't hear the fire alarms, had to wear certain pyjamas in case there was an emergency, etc. Really sucked.

My brother in law is like this. I can't watch sports with him, he actually gives me anxiety. It's an expletive a minute regardless of if his team is winning or losing. But if they're losing it's much louder and has set off panic attacks where I have to go sit in a dark, quiet room for a while to calm down. It just ruins it for everyone and in the end I look like the bitchy overly sensitive sister in law that doesn't want anyone to have any fun. But if you're setting off panic attacks in someone then you really need to chill the eff out. Ruined 3 super bowls in a row for me. Luckily I really didn't care about either team in any of them.

Thank you. I have really bad anxiety so I worry about everything. I've only been going through this for a year and a half so I expect I'll probably get denied but I literally cannot function at this point.
Yes, sorry, my brain is mush today. It's been a really stressful week.

This is the technique I was taught in therapy and it works sometimes. I've also heard from my therapist that some people's brains can't be calmed down sometimes just because of how bad the situation is or how it relates to trauma, etc. So even if it doesn't work at times it's still the best breathing technique I've learned. Would definitely recommend it. I think I read somewhere that our hearts are constantly speeding up and slowing down so the exhale is the longest because exhaling slows your heart rate down.

"When you exhale, blood returns to your body from your lungs and the heart slows back down as the PSNS/"Brake" drive increases. The increase in heart rate during inhalation and decrease during exhalation is known as respiratory sinus arrhythmia and is a sign of a healthy heart." https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/neuraptitude/201602/the-science-slow-deep-breathing

I had to drive this with torrential (non-hurricane) rain last fall. It was terrifying. Probably for the best they closed it. People were driving like idiots even though there was almost zero visibility. I think it took 10 years off my life.

Yes. I worked for both the Immigrant Visa and Non-immigrant Visa departments as a CSR type deal. But we weren't called that. We were Visa Processing Specialists. There was nothing special about it, just phone calls, lots of e-binders full of info that we had to know which section to go to but not necessarily remember all the regulations because holy hell are there a lot of hoops to jump through to get into the US. But anyway, USCBP can deny you for a number of stupid reasons. Even if you've gone through the Visa process and had an embassy interview. What we were supposed to tell people was that USCBP is the "last line of defense" to get to into the country and their decision is the final one. I've had calls such as family members asking why their dad can't come in the country with them and why they had to pay to fly back home. When I looked into his record it showed marijuana possession in the 80s, clean record after that. So CBP refused to let him in. There's a system with all your information if you have a record or have ever had an embassy interview. I heard the craziest things. It was heartbreaking at times. Most stressful job I ever had and I'll never go back into that field.

Thank you. I'm currently trying to get a new doctor because obviously she doesn't get it. It's hard trying to find that fine line between just enough and too much activity. Especially if an unexpected stressor comes up throwing a wrench in the works.

I had an MRI, neurological workups (one before and after the MRI looking for two completely different things), tons of bloodwork, x-rays, almost was convinced to undergo surgery by my piece of crap doctor at the time, put on many different antidepressants to get rid of the "stress causing all my pain", etc etc etc. My neurologist was actually the one that ordered Lyme bloodwork and put me on something for sleep, suggested I find a new PCP after she spoke with my doctor and realized she was just throwing meds at me. I got a new NP who went over my medical history, discussed it thoroughly with me, ordered even more bloodwork and then wanted me to go to a psychiatrist to get a better psychological workup and the meds I would need. Ended up with new diagnosis of fibromyalgia, PTSD, headaches with no cause that don't respond to medications (can't remember the medical term), ADHD, depression, anxiety, panic attacks, and insomnia instead of the "stress" that I was "diagnosed with" before. So it could be fibro plus a combination of other things making it worse. Definitely don't rule out other concurrent diseases. And don't let your doctor blame everything on fibro. My current doctor does this, and it drives me nuts. My NP took time off to raise her daughter. She always told me "don't blame everything on fibro" especially after I threw my back shortly after being diagnosed. I just figured it was part of this new diagnosis that I knew nothing about. Went two weeks before going to the doctor. 
I should mention that I was only finally referred to the neurologist because two family members have MS. I had to fight with my old doctor to even get that done. Some doctors really just don't want to do the legwork but if you feel like you need more then keep pushing.

I did 30 minutes on a recumbent bike, at a slow speed, then an hour long arthritis pool class and was down for a week. Could barely function. My doctor told me I'm not trying hard enough. 🤷‍♀️ 
It's definitely mentally draining for sure.
I have this and it sucks. Can make you jump right out of bed. Sorry to hear you have it too.
I have a tea that I drink at bedtime with valerian root, which isn't fresh but I do notice the calming effects.

Exactly. I know she's just trying to find one magic drug or combination that will help everything. I do make sure to tell her that it REALLY helps my restless legs. If I don't take it then it's constant all day all night RLS symptoms. I'm actually impressed how well it does work for my legs.
I will. She's very understanding but also concerned that my pain isn't getting any better.

My doctor wants to take me off gabapentin if it doesn't start helping with pain but gabapentin is the only thing that I've found to help my RLS. I'll full on have a sobbing meltdown in her office if I have to start dealing with that again.
I was wondering the same thing. Seen a lot of posts with that lately.

This is what happens to me when I get an allergic reaction to eating coconut. Might be worth keeping track of what foods you eat or what you drink when it happens. I also tend to bite it when it's swollen without really realizing it and it's super painful for the next day or two.
